record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Can one prove full input-to-state stability, without any restriction on input magnitude, for the Burgers equation x_t = μ x_{zz} − ν x x_z on z ∈ (0,1) with boundary conditions x(t,0)=0 and x(t,1)=u(t), when the state is measured in L2(0,1) and the input belongs to a bounded piecewise-continuous input space such as P Cb(R+, R)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.12. Is it possible to prove ISS of Burgers’ equation (5.40)-(5.41) with X := L2(0, 1) and u ∈ P Cb(R+, R) (or for another input space) without restrictions on the magnitude of inputs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the viscous Burgers equation on the spatial interval $(0,1)$ with boundary control:
$$x_t(t,z) = \mu\, x_{zz}(t,z) - \nu\, x(t,z)\, x_z(t,z), \qquad t>0,\ z\in(0,1),$$
$$x(t,0) = 0, \qquad x(t,1) = u(t), \qquad t \ge 0,$$
with constants $\mu>0$, $\nu>0$, initial condition $x(0,\cdot)\in L^2(0,1)$, and input $u$ in the space $PC_b(\mathbb{R}_+,\mathbb{R})$ of bounded piecewise-continuous real-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}_+$, equipped with the supremum norm.

The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) with respect to the state space $X := L^2(0,1)$ and the input space $\mathcal{U} := PC_b(\mathbb{R}_+,\mathbb{R})$ if there exist functions $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma \in \mathcal{K}$ such that for every initial state $x_0 \in L^2(0,1)$ and every input $u \in \mathcal{U}$ the corresponding (mild) solution satisfies
$$\|x(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2(0,1)} \le \beta\bigl(\|x_0\|_{L^2(0,1)},\, t\bigr) + \gamma\bigl(\|u\|_{\infty}\bigr) \qquad \text{for all } t \ge 0,$$
with no a priori restriction on the magnitude of $\|x_0\|_{L^2(0,1)}$ or $\|u\|_{\infty}$.

Question: Prove or disprove that the above boundary-controlled viscous Burgers equation is input-to-state stable in this sense, without any restriction on the magnitude of inputs (or, more generally, decide ISS for some other natural input space in place of $PC_b(\mathbb{R}_+,\mathbb{R})$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as Open Problem 5.12 in the 2020 SIAM Review survey by Mironchenko and Prieur. Subsequent work (e.g., Zheng–Zhu) establishes ISS/iISS in $L^q$ norms for generalized Burgers-type equations with boundary disturbances under various conditions, and local/De-Giorgi-iteration based ISS results are known, but no published result establishes full (global, unrestricted-magnitude) ISS in $L^2(0,1)$ with $PC_b$ boundary inputs for the standard viscous Burgers equation. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems: Recent Results and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 5.12. Is it possible to prove ISS of Burgers' equation with X:=L2(0,1) and u in PC_b(R+,R) (or for another input space) without restrictions on the magnitude of inputs?
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as an open problem in the survey.

status_evidence.title: ISS with Respect to In-domain and Boundary Disturbances for a Generalized Burgers' Equation
status_evidence.snippet: ISS and iISS in L^q-norm (q>=2) with respect to in-domain and boundary disturbances for a generalized Burgers' equation with higher-order nonlinearities have been established.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for generalized Burgers equations, but does not resolve the standard L^2 case without magnitude restriction.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic ISS Lyapunov functions for linear analytic systems
status_evidence.snippet: No coercive ISS Lyapunov function is known for this Burgers system, and existence of such a function is neither proved nor disproved.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the question remains unresolved in subsequent literature.
